lesson.child_mission: Food advertising uses colour, characters, slogans and health claims to persuade; smart consumers check labels and ask what is missing.
lesson.evidence_instructions: Save the independent response, specific revisions and both short-answer explanations; record oral evidence for speaking tasks.
lesson.extension: Apply the same idea to a new game or situation, then compare two choices for safety and inclusion.
lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Name two advertising tricks and one check you should do.

FEEDBACK
e.g. cartoon/bright colours; check sugar on label.

WATCH FOR
Believing every “healthy” slogan is proven is risky.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Analyse three ads: techniques, claim, label check. Write a sceptic question for each.

Write a short reflection naming one choice you changed and why. Any movement is optional, adult-supervised and can be done in a gentler way or described instead.
lesson.learning_intention: Food advertising uses colour, characters, slogans and health claims to persuade; smart consumers check labels and ask what is missing.
materials: Clear, safe movement space with an adult nearby for any physical activity
Optional: soft ball, cushion or water bottle
lesson.offline_alternative: Use paper and pencil to complete the original task, then retain a photograph or short parent observation as evidence.
lesson.parent_notes:
Parent: Marking guidance for the independent task: Analyse three ads: techniques, claim, label check. Write a sceptic question for each. Accept equivalent original responses that show the same skill.

Parent: Written model 1: Sample: original example using advertising on new material; names a specific word, source or choice and explains its effect.

Parent: Written model 2: Sample error: Believing every “healthy” slogan is proven is risky.. Correction: e.g. cartoon/bright colours;. Why it helps the audience is stated.

Parent: Likely misconception: Believing every “healthy” slogan is proven is risky. Keep sample answers out of the child role.

Parent: Short-answer focus 1: Produce a fresh example demonstrating advertising on new material (not the worked model). Explain the particular words, sources or choices that make it work.

Parent: Short-answer focus 2: Name one likely error with advertising, correct it, and explain why the correction helps a reader or audience.

Parent: Marking notes: Accept original work about advertising with a specific supporting detail. Reject copied model wording with no new material. / Accept a misconception, a correction, and a purpose-linked reason for advertising. Reject corrections that do not change the inaccurate idea..

teach_steps.explain:
Food advertising uses colour, characters, slogans and health claims to persuade; smart consumers check labels and ask what is missing.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make safe, healthy and respectful choices using clear cues and reasons, rather than guessing or copying others. Every choice keeps bodies safe and includes everyone.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the cues, rules or choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For any movement, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby, move at your own comfortable level and stop if anything hurts or feels unsafe. You may always choose a gentler version or only describe the movement. One deliberate, reasoned change is more useful than a longer answer.
